comment: Written by node scripts/sources/build.mjs from adapters/*/source.json; never edited by hand. Sorted by bit, then the sources with no bit by id.

failure_modes: The file is late: it lands at about 00:02 to 00:05 UTC the next day (MEASURED 2026-11-01, DOM-029), and the hourly run reads it then. A day not written by D+1 06:00Z goes to the cursor's open list, so the days after it are read as they land, and the daily compaction stops waiting for it; a file that lands after its day pack was built is absorbed into that day pack by the next daily.

The file never comes: a day not written by D+2 12:00Z is declared a gap, which reaches the root's gaps through state (2026-10-04 and 2026-10-09 so far). A gap is never final: a later backfill dispatch that finds the day adds its segments, and the promotion drops the gap.

One host fails, times out after 900 s or answers 404: the other host is read in the same run, cs2 first for the live day and the bucket first for a backfill. A listing of the bucket that fails is a fault, never an absence.
Every host fails: one fault line a host, the cursor kept, and the next hour's run tries again; a day still unwritten at D+2 12:00Z becomes a gap.

A body shorter or longer than its length, a Content-Encoding, a truncated gzip or a second gzip member, or a file over 2 GiB: the faults length, encoding, gzip and size. Each host is taken through its whole integrity pass before anything is written, so nothing is written from a host that faults.

An empty file, or a changed line format: the fault empty when no name is kept, and format when more than half of the non-empty lines are refused; from 1% refused the share is a stat the workflow warns on (0.018% measured, all address literals; MEASURED 2026-11-01, DOM-029).

The volume shifts without notice (September 843 to 986 MB a day, October 77 to 984 MB): the band is 0.4 to 4 times the median of the last 7 accepted days, a day outside it on either side is quarantined (served, never as new), and 3 consecutive days on one side reset the baseline (the replay of the 59 days quarantines 2026-10-05, 10-06 and 10-15; MEASURED 2026-11-01, DOM-029).
The order is a locale collation, not bytes (24.5% of adjacent lines inverted in the head of 2026-10-31; MEASURED 2026-11-01, DOM-029): the adapter sorts the keys itself, in runs merged by a heap.
Upper case on 0.6 to 1.0% of the lines: lowercased by the names package.
CRLF line endings: one trailing carriage return is stripped from a line and counted (none measured); a carriage return inside a line is refused as charset.
Address literals such as 192.0.2.1, which a certificate carried: refused as numeric-tld and counted.

The bucket's directory is the month the file was uploaded, not the month of its date: 2026-10-31 sits at 2026/11/2026-10-31.txt.gz (MEASURED 2026-11-01, DOM-029). The path is always taken from the bucket's listing, never built from the date.

Port 9092 does not answer or the broker stops: the fault broker fails the kafka leg, the cursor holds, and the next run reads the backlog from the stored offset. P6D is a declared floor, READ from two offset readings (2026-10-28 and 2026-10-31, DOM-026): the broker deletes whole segments of about 7 days.

The cursor falls below the earliest retained offset: the fault retention-gap names the lost offsets and times, and the read resumes at the earliest retained offset with a fresh window. The lost days become a gap of the root only by --gap of scripts/root/promote.mjs, which no workflow passes yet (DOM-034), and until then the source's later packs wait.

The log changes under the cursor (an offset above the latest, or a first record more than an hour before the cursor's through): the fault offset-ahead or cursor-mismatch, and the read relocates to the first offset whose record time is at or after through.

A batch fails its CRC-32C, or is compressed with a codec other than none or snappy: the fault decode, and the topic stops before that batch on every run until a code change reads it or the retention deletes it; the leg is red every run.

A record time more than 300 s after the run's time: the fault clock, and the topic stops before that record until the clock passes it. A record time before 2026-01-01, which no record stores: the fault clock-low, and the record joins its window at the window's start, counted late.
A message is not JSON or lacks its name: counted malformed, one fault a run; the window is written and the raw lane keeps the bytes.

Zone rows (ct_name zone_data, no registration date) arrive in registry bursts: 33.5% of the topic over the retained span (1,294,264 of 3,866,241 messages), up to 95.1% of an hour, and 140,503 messages in one minute (MEASURED 2026-10-31, DOM-026). Each is T2 nrd-list, and a window closes early at a second once it holds 200,000 messages.

Between a third and a half of the events carry a certificate older than 7 days, by sample (51.1% of the newest 19,951 with both times, 32.5% of the earliest; MEASURED 2026-10-31, DOM-026): the minimum age of a key goes to facts.json, and the feed marks the row suspect.

The JSON timestamp of this topic steps back up to 25,556 s over the retained span (8,389 s in the newest 20,000 messages; MEASURED 2026-10-31, DOM-026), so windows are cut on the Kafka record time.
A message is not JSON, lacks its name, or holds a confidence that is not a whole number from 1 to 10: counted malformed, one fault a run; the raw lane keeps the bytes.

Zone rows (ct_name zone_data, no certificate) are 25.2% of the retained span (476,562 of 1,894,990 messages), up to 91.4% of an hour, in registry bursts, 95.4% of them with confidence 8 to 10 (MEASURED 2026-10-31, DOM-026): each is T2 nrd-list with its confidence, and only a row with a certificate is nrd-ct+rdap. The topic has no submission_timestamp, so no certificate age.
